subject.title: [Feature]: Enrich message_sending hook with resolved target context

question: What resolved outbound target facts may ordinary loaded plugins receive on `message_sending`, and should that contract be nested as `targetContext` or exposed through a different Plugin SDK shape?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the next step defines a public Plugin SDK contract and a security disclosure boundary for channel/account/cross-context information.

options.title: Approve a narrow target context
options.body: Expose only stable, policy-useful facts such as target kind, channel id, and cross-context/external booleans, populated from existing outbound resolver and policy state.

options.title: Keep the hook raw for now
options.body: Leave `message_sending` unchanged until a broader plugin policy/trust model decides what target-resolution details plugins may observe.

options.title: Use an explicit resolver helper instead
options.body: Document a supported plugin-side resolver path, accepting that plugins may need to opt into lookup cost and may not see the exact runtime-resolved destination for every send.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow target context
recommendation.body: Expose only stable, policy-useful facts such as target kind, channel id, and cross-context/external booleans, populated from existing outbound resolver and policy state.

likelyOwner.reason: History connects this account to both the target-resolution/outbound-policy internals and the plugin API/product boundary that need the decision.
